title: Optimal prophet-secretary constant
formal: Determine the optimal prophet-secretary constant α_PS for independent nonnegative integrable values arriving in uniformly random order with identities revealed.
definitions: For each n≥1 let X_1,…,X_n be independent nonnegative real random variables of known Borel laws with 0<E[max_i X_i]<∞. A uniform random permutation, independent of all values, presents the pairs (i,X_i) sequentially. The decision-maker knows n and the full laws, observes identities and values as they arrive, and may accept at most one value irrevocably. Rejection is permanent; accepting none gives zero. Policies may be randomized and may perform unrestricted computation; they must be measurable functions of observed histories and independent private randomness. Atoms and ties in values are permitted and may be handled by the policy. For each instance I let v(I) be the supremum expected selected value over these policies. Define α_PS=inf_I v(I)/E[max_i X_i], with the infimum over every n and all such laws. This instance-wise optimum formulation permits arbitrarily approaching an unattained supremum.
answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute distance from the defined optimal ratio is at most 1/100. Certified upper and lower bounds with gap at most 1/50 qualify via their midpoint. Bounds must cover all instances and all competing policies as quantified; attaining the infimum or supremum is not required.
context: The 2024 preprint improves the general single-selection guarantee to 0.688; the matching extension is a different optimization problem.
why: The prophet-secretary constant quantifies the value of distribution knowledge under random arrival.

import_provenance.original_statement: What is the largest universal α such that, for independent nonnegative values drawn from known distributions and revealed in uniformly random order, an online algorithm selecting at most one value guarantees α times the expected maximum? Closing this optimal-stopping gap continues the random-arrival problem studied in Vredeveld and coauthors’ work and survey.

sentences: Independent values come from known distributions.
Their arrival order is uniform and independent of the samples.
The policy observes both identity and value before accepting or rejecting.
Only one value can be selected and past rejections cannot be recalled.
The benchmark is the expected maximum and the target is the optimal universal factor.
